title: Harding Rewrites Winton's Quant Playbook in Search for Returns

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Harding Rewrites Winton's Quant Playbook in Search for Returns.docx

summary: Bloomberg TV (Mar 2019) interview with Winton founder David Harding on why systematic strategies struggle. Trend following in futures became crowded, near-zero rates cut hedge fund returns, so Winton shifted to equity event, organizational-metric and technical strategies across 7000 stocks. Warns government data are unreliable and trend following is not a crash hedge.

coverage.note: low rates and crowding, innovation, 7000 stock portfolios, high-frequency data
crowded trend following, jungle model, edge decay, leverage and catastrophe risk
leverage, future of quant, agricultural futures
weather/long data, government data revisions, PMI study, equity strategies
momentum transfer, AI hype, responsibility, trend following forecast lowered
trend Sharpe, new strategies, client redemptions
fee and liquidity terms, hedge fund beta, competitors
volatility not rising, trend following as hedge, future of discretionary

completeness_estimate: 0.94 - first reader captured essentially all mechanisms, research findings and risk methods accurately; missed only the no-discretionary-intervention governance rule and the reason redemption terms were lengthened (asset liquidity)

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: with very low in low to zero interest rates um it's pretty tough to make money in the hedge fund game at the moment
claims.claim: Hedge fund returns are weak when interest rates are near zero (no cash return) and strategies are crowded, deteriorating return-to-risk.
claims.indicator: policy interest rate level; strategy crowding
claims.testable: partly - compare fund returns vs cash rate

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: any business that succeeds and isn't a monopoly tends to get too much capital applied to it that's what drives innovation
claims.claim: Successful strategies attract too much capital, driving returns down and forcing innovation.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: we use short-term data even though we don't
claims.claim: Uses high-frequency data to measure correlation changes and emergence of new factors even though trading is long term; computing in the cloud allowed portfolios of 7000 stocks (from ~1000-1500 five years ago), now a third to a half of weight.
claims.indicator: intraday data for correlation and factor emergence

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the faster strategies got very crowded in futures many many years ago we managed to avoid that by getting slower but even the slower strategies i fear are beginning to get a bit crowded now
claims.claim: Trend following in futures has become crowded and is seen as beta: fast versions crowded first, slower ones now, so returns shrink and the firm shifted toward equity strategies.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: they're more like a kind of thriving ecosystem jungle
claims.claim: Markets are an evolving ecosystem, not a perfectly efficient system; edges decay but new ones emerge, so innovation is needed.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the two and twenty day moving average crossover system you would have made that like a bandit in the 80s
claims.claim: A simple 2/20-day moving-average crossover made large returns in the 1980s, which no longer works the same way, showing edge decay in simple trend rules.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: for most of the 80s and 90s risk-free rates were six so hedge funds had six percent added in
claims.claim: Today's lower hedge fund returns partly reflect near-zero cash rates (6% in 80s-90s) and halved leverage; doubling track record and adding 6% looks similar to the past.
claims.testable: yes - compare returns net of cash and leverage

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the crowdedness creates the the risk of catastrophe the risk of an overnight massive move
claims.claim: Leverage cut because crowdedness plus fat tails creates risk of overnight catastrophic moves (LTCM, 2008); responsible managers avoid systemic risk.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: our leverage in a similar portfolio would be a fraction of that two times instead of ten times
claims.claim: Uses about 2x gross leverage in long-short portfolios, versus ~10x rumoured for Goldman Global Alpha, conservative especially when serving less sophisticated clients.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the markets are not going to suddenly become efficient and then all you know quantitative strategy managers are going to disappear mysteriously
claims.claim: Quant investing has a bigger future because markets will not become efficient; competition is fierce but spurs progress and finance is not a natural monopoly.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: we can't afford to move those markets we can't afford to move in and out with a scale of capital we're operating on we have to be taking big long-term positions
claims.claim: Agricultural futures work uses very long-term strategies because capacity is limited and large capital cannot trade in and out.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: in the case of the grains we have data going back 1 200 years
claims.claim: Grain price data go back 1,200 years; researching weather changes and long time series could underpin an ag trading system (not yet found).

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: it's always been difficult using you know government produced statistics in countries has always been difficult because they're revised so often
claims.claim: Government economic statistics are revised heavily (US 2009 double dip erased nine years later; Japan growth 0.4 vs 2.5), so real-time fundamental data are untrustworthy for systematic macro.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: we spent perhaps two years and several million pounds to try and it was totally inconclusive
claims.claim: A long-run study of the PMI as a forecaster of the economy for betting on stock industries had too little data to prove anything after two years and millions in cost, and sunk cost should not force a result.
claims.testable: yes - insufficient data is itself the finding

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: just taking futures trend following systems and applying them to um equities doesn't work at all
claims.claim: Futures trend-following systems applied unchanged to equities fail; equity strategies need event, organizational/governance metrics and customised technical strategies across 7000 stocks.
claims.indicator: trend following signal on single stocks
claims.testable: yes - backtest futures trend on stocks

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: there is some of our knowledge of how to trade momentum in futures that has been applicable to our global equity technical
claims.claim: Some momentum know-how from futures carries over to global equity technical strategies.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: one part reality and nine parts hype
claims.claim: AI view: deep learning has made progress but is not general intelligence; there is 1 part reality and 9 parts hype; responsibility for algorithms must stay with named humans.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: i've been lowering my forecast for the success of trend following year by year for years and years
claims.claim: Trend following should be expected to make less money over time, so he has lowered expectations yearly and diversified into other strategies, not abandoned it.
claims.testable: partly - forecast decay of trend returns

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: we had a short ratio of best nearly one for 30 years
claims.claim: Trend following delivered a Sharpe ratio near 1 for 30 years but too much money and competition now; innovators survive.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the systems we're moving into have the same properties as trend flow in other words they're unpredictable they're statistical systems we can't forecast when they're going to work
claims.claim: New strategies are statistical like trend following: they cannot be forecast to work in a given period, so diversification and a long horizon matter; judge managers over many years not months.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: we've always historically as part of the sort of futures uh uh tradition we've always charged quarterly performance fees and now that's nearly all annual
claims.claim: Fee and liquidity terms moved to monthly notice and annual crystallisation, with management fee cut from 1% to 0.9% and performance fee from 20% to 16% as returns did not justify fees.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: hedge fund industry gets quite a lot of uh knock-on benefit from
claims.claim: Hedge fund returns were sustained by the equity bull market beta spillover.
claims.testable: yes - hedge fund returns vs equity beta

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the fact that we are exclusively focused on managing money for clients as opposed to having also managing our own money is very attractive
claims.claim: Aligned business: focused solely on client money, relevant to institutions.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: they have a large body of world-beating scientists who have carried out a research project and built a cumulative body of intellectual property
claims.claim: Renaissance's edge is cumulative scientific research by a large team over ~20 years, not a single data item or magic number.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: we broadly control our volatility by setting the level of gearing there it is almost as simple as there being one number
claims.claim: Volatility is controlled by a single leverage 'volume knob' (10, 20 or 30 vol), independent of strategy changes.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: a storm is people thought a storm was coming but they couldn't imagine what the storm was going to be
claims.claim: Prolonged low volatility (2006-07) preceded the financial crisis; volatility spikes (2016 vol derivatives, 2018) hurt returns and cannot be solved for.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the idea that the markets are getting more volatile um is a silly idea really
claims.claim: Volatility is not rising: measured in percent, 1933-34 was the highest; point-based charts mislead, so use log charts.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: if the market crashed the ctas we're going to lose a lot of money
claims.claim: Trend following is not a reliable hedge: it hedged in 2008, 2001-02, but in a 1987-style crash or Feb 2018 managed futures funds were long and lost because trends were up.
claims.conditions: sudden crash after a long uptrend

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the future is bad for anyone who hasn't isn't adding real value
claims.claim: Active managers without real edge face pressure from data and performance evaluation; many discretionary strategies are simpler than thought and can be automated, as trend following was.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: the algorithm that's done the money making for assist is not very intelligent because um you didn't have to be very intelligent to make money
claims.claim: Simple trend algorithm produced ~15% compounded for 20 years, showing intelligence is not what limits returns.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: it does the messy tedious work of organizing and cleaning data series so that you can do research into those data series
claims.claim: Spun off the data-cleaning business (Hivemind) because clean data are the unglamorous prerequisite for research and AI training.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: now you can just rent you know 50 000 computers for a minute
claims.claim: Cloud computing lets him rent huge compute for a short time for large experiments instead of owning machines, making research more efficient.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: we have no intellectual property protection unlike you know the software business
claims.claim: No IP protection and no publication in quant finance means advances are kept secret and knowledge progresses slowly; he expects the word quant to disappear as everyone uses computers.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: if the program you know miscalculated something we would um you know we would do something we we are responsible for managing the money
claims.claim: Governance of a fully systematic book: researchers write and run the programs, execution is done by separate teams, and humans step in only to correct program errors, not to override signals with discretionary views.

claims.speaker: David Harding
claims.quote: our own funds have moved more into line with other hedge funds having you know having more no longer notice period says because they got more investments in small companies
claims.claim: Fund redemption terms were lengthened (monthly notice, less liquid than before) because the strategy mix now holds more small-company equities, matching investor liquidity to the liquidity of the assets.
claims.indicator: fund notice period vs asset liquidity
claims.conditions: shift from liquid futures to broader equity universes
